messages:
derek: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel bump to 6.x we saw a spike in CPU on the KV pager hosts. Flamegraphs point at `mmap_slab_free` / `msync` hot paths. Repro trace + quick notes below.

priya: ugh, saw alerts too. Are these the nodes doing small-window chat workloads?

matt: yep, mostly many short sequences + high QPS (300-800/s). Paging + slab handoff seems to thrash.

olga: can you paste the flame snippet?

perf-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T22:14:02 -> kernel 6.x; hosts: pager-*-prod; anomaly score 7.4.

matt: ```
# perf top sample (aggregated)
80.2%  [kernel]      mmap_slab_free
5.1%   runtime         kv_cache_free
4.7%   libc            msync
3.0%   runtime         slotmap_reclaim
```

derek: Minimal repro steps i used: start small-window generator with seq_len mean=16, concurrency 120, prefix caching disabled. Observed 2x tail latency and CPU up ~40%.

priya: hypothesis: the new kernel changed mmap hinting and `msync` behavior, causing our slab to flush more often when pages are returned to OS. That interacts badly with our slab->mmap handoff path.

olga: also saw fragmentation increasing in telemetry: free-slab-chunks drops while mmap-backed pages climb. Could be our hybrid allocator fallback frequency increasing.

matt: quick mitigations I tried: 1) increase slab reuse window (avoid immediate munmap) 2) coalesce frees on background thread 3) enable `MADV_DONTNEED` instead of msync for hot path — reduced CPU but risky.

priya: can you paste the coalesce sketch?

matt: ```rust
// pseudo
fn deferred_free(chunk) {
  deferred_queue.push(chunk);
  if deferred_queue.len() > COALESCE_THRESH {
    drain_and_return(deferred_queue.drain(..));
  }
}
```

derek: perf numbers after coalescing: CPU down ~18%, tail latency back ~10-15%. But memory footprint rose ~6% for short bursts.

olga: we should add telemetry hooks: counter for deferred-queue-length, msync-count, madvise-count, and per-host slab-frag-percent. Agree?

priya: yes. Also need a kernel-compat toggle in runtime config to prefer MADV_DONTNEED vs msync per host. Rollout can be canaryed.

matt: I'll open a tiny RFC with upgrade plan + config flag. For immediate safety, recommend canary 10% of pager hosts with `deferred_free` enabled and `madvise` fallback.

derek: also add a microbenchmark: many short seqs + frequent KV eviction to measure slab churn and msync rate. Put it under infra/perf so we can run nightly.

olga: logged: https://perf.example.com/notes/3765012345-mmap-slab-handoff (private) with raw flamegraphs and histograms.

perf-bot: note: created ticket INF-1971 for canary rollout + telemetry.

priya: thanks. @matt can you paste the canary config snippet when you make the RFC?

matt: will do in RFC. TL;DR: deferred_free=true, deferred_threshold=64, free-mode=madvise, canary=0.1

derek: sounds good. If we still see regressions after canary, plan B is to revert kernel on affected pool or move those workloads to dedicated slab-only nodes.

olga: agree. Also add a guard in the allocator: if msync latency > 5ms for 1m window, auto-switch to madvise on that host.

priya: added to RFC TODOs. Closing provisional action items: (1) RFC for deferred_free + canary (matt) (2) telemetry counters (olga) (3) microbench harness (derek) (4) INF ticket monitoring (perf-bot).

matt: ping me if you want to run the canary on testpool first.

derek: thanks all :thumbsup:
